newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL SOCIEDAD ONLY FIRST DIVISION VICTIM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL SOCIEDAD ONLY FIRST DIVISION VICTIM.

text.p: Real Sociedad will be the only big name missing from the third round of the Spanish Cup after all other 14 first division sides involved in second round, second leg action came through unscathed on Wednesday.
Real Sociedad could only manage a 1-1 draw with Osasuna after losing the first leg 1-0, while Deportivo Coruna came back from a 1-0 defeat at Mallorca with a convincing 3-0 win.
Real Madrid repeated the 2-0 first leg win over Salamanca, while bottom-placed Extremadura turned round a 1-0 defeat by runaway second division leaders Merida into a crushing 5-1 victory.

Rayo Vallecano beat Albacete by the same score after a 0-0 draw in the away game, and goalless draws were enough for both Logrones and Racing Santander to go through on the away goals rule after 1-1 draws in their respective first legs against Alaves and Eibar.

On the day he was named to preside next week's Real Madrid-Barcelona league fixture, controversial referee Brito Arceo walked into a deluge of criticism after failing to award a clear penalty in Sevilla's goalless draw with Malaga.
Sevilla won the game 1-0 on aggregate, while neighbours Real Betis defeated Ecija 2-0, and 4-1 on aggregate.
